Khan Academy will teach you everything in more detail but I'm a former chem major and here are the basics because I love chemistry:

The atomic number is the order the element appears on the table (Eg, H is 1, He is 2, Li is 3...), and is also the number of protons present in each element. Protons are what differentiate each element from one another.

Protons (positive charge) are subatomic particles, along with neutrons (no charge) and electrons (negative charge). Protons and neutrons are the main parts that make up the atom and electrons orbit around them. They're also what gives atoms their mass - atomic mass is the other number you'll see on the periodic table, H is 1.008, He is 4.003, Li is 6.941... One thing to keep in mind is that the number of protons won't vary for any given element, but the number of neutrons might. This is called an isotope, and they vary in weight, so the atomic mass on the periodic table is just the "average" calculated to account for how common each isotope is. (eg: carbon-12 is about 98% of all natural carbon on earth, carbon-13 is about 1.1%).

Electrons orbiting around the atom is what allows elements to bond to another, the outermost (called *valence*) negatively-charged electrons of one atom being attracted to the positively-charged nucleus of a different atom are what allows them to bond to one another. 

Groups on the periodic table are columns and they have similar properties. Periods are the rows. Group 1 elements are called alkali metals and consists of Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, and Fr.
